analysis: What changed versus the 6:00 AM brief: the cash open turned the overnight shock into a real tape — NVDA opened down 13.4% ($150.49, ~$560B of market value gone at the open) and then bounced hard, trading $162.23 (-6.6%) by 9:52 AM ET after an intraday low of $148.80. The bounce, not the open, is the signal: buyers stepped in once the 8-K confirmed the board accepted Huang's resignation on Nov 11 and earnings stay on schedule for Nov 17. The rest of the tape refused to follow Nvidia down — AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL and TSLA were all green by mid-morning, AMZN +2.3%, and the S&P pared its opening -0.77% to about -0.30% by 9:45 AM ET, with the Dow flipping positive. The damage stayed inside the AI complex: NBIS -16.9% on the funding math, and the Nvidia-funded names (Micron, Intel, Dell, ARM, Oracle) down 3-9%, while AMD and Broadcom extended their rotation gains. Oppenheimer's downgrade to Market Perform adds to the Bernstein/Morgan Stanley reset — Wall Street is now pricing a leadership discount, not a demand problem. Signal vs noise: the resignation, the 8-K, and the earnings date are confirmed signal; AI-generated blogs denying the resignation that circulated this morning are stale noise; the HN resignation thread (40 comments so far) is thin next to the 1,545-comment ouster thread from overnight. The open's message is containment so far — one stock's crisis, not a market one — but the QQQ slipped just under its 200-day ($680.57 vs $681.71) and the VIX is up ~1.5 points, so the tape is fragile into Cisco and Applied Materials after the close.

community_signals.takeaway: Fresh thread on the confirmed resignation; discussion is shifting from whether Huang would go to succession — who replaces him, whether Kress stays interim through the Nov 17 earnings print, and what the leadership vacuum means for AI chip strategy.
community_signals.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after reports of second affair deepened scandal

headlines.headline: Nvidia opened down 13.4% at $150.49 shortly after the 9:30 AM ET open (vs Wednesday's $173.73 close), wiping out roughly $560B of market value, then bounced to $162.23 (-6.62%) by 9:52 AM ET after an intraday low of $148.80. Nvidia's SEC Form 8-K confirms the board accepted Huang's resignation on Nov 11, effective immediately, and the company confirmed fiscal Q3 earnings remain scheduled for Nov 17 (results ~1:20 PM PT, call 2:00 PM PT).
headlines.why_it_matters: The open was the panic print and the bounce is the read — buyers stepped in once the 8-K and the Nov 17 earnings date removed the worst uncertainty, so the move is now about the leadership discount, not a demand problem.

headlines.headline: Oppenheimer downgraded Nvidia to Market Perform from Outperform (MarketBeat, Nov 12), adding to Bernstein's price-target cut to $200 from $400 and Morgan Stanley dropping NVDA from its top-pick list. One Bloomberg-cited estimate put Nvidia's fair value without Huang at about $225 a share, against $300 if he stays.
headlines.why_it_matters: Wall Street is now explicitly pricing a 'Huang discount' into the stock — the downgrades frame this as a valuation reset on leadership, which caps how far the morning bounce can run without a successor name.

headlines.headline: Stocks opened lower and pared losses in the first 30 minutes: at the open the Dow was +0.11%, S&P 500 -0.77% and Nasdaq Composite -1.51%; by ~9:25 AM ET (15-min delayed) SPY was $754.69 (-0.67%), QQQ $680.57 (-1.44%) and DIA $523.25 (-0.23%); by 9:45 AM ET the S&P 500 was -0.30% at 7,594.68, the Nasdaq -0.56% at 25,321.71 and the Dow +0.06% at 52,509.67. VIX 18.99 (+8.64% on the day, vs Wednesday's 17.49 close).
headlines.why_it_matters: The open gave back part of Wednesday's +1.31% S&P rally but the tape stabilized fast — the Dow flipping positive shows the selling is concentrated in AI names, not broad-based.

headlines.headline: The chip split carried into the cash session: at the open AMD rose 2.54% and Broadcom advanced 3.7% on rotation, while TSMC dropped 3.73%, Micron fell 4.65%, Intel declined 4.11%, Oracle fell 2.91%, Dell plunged 8.66% and ARM fell 5.21%. Nebius (NBIS) was among the day's biggest losers at -16.9% after the earnings call put 2027 capex of $40-45B against $12-13B of revenue guidance.
headlines.why_it_matters: Traders are rotating within AI, not out of it — rivals gain on share-gain hopes while Nvidia-funded names fall on funding fears, so the open is a stock-picking tape, not a sector rout.

headlines.headline: The other megacaps held up in the first half-hour: as of ~9:52-9:54 AM ET, Amazon $272.30 (+2.30%), Alphabet $296.38 (+1.00%), Tesla $395.28 (+1.14%), Microsoft $525.07 (+0.76%) and Apple $357.53 (+0.53%) were all higher, while Meta $625.13 (-0.58%) was the only megacap loser. Meta fell 1.97% Wednesday after the WSJ reported United Airlines plans to block personal AI assistants from its booking systems.
headlines.why_it_matters: Five of six megacaps green while NVDA is down double digits is the containment read — the market is treating this as a single-company governance shock, not a megacap re-rating.
